The billets were held at 1200 ◦ C for 60 min, and then quenched in water.

Diffusion-controlled precipitation dominates in high-temperature forging, while coupled diffusion-controlled and dislocation-assisted nucleation dominates in low-temperature forging.
At 900 ◦ C, silicides nucleate from the α / β phase boundaries through discontinuous nucleation, relying on Si and Zr diffusion along grain boundaries.
At lower temperatures (800 ◦ C), reduced grain size and high dislocation density increase nucleation sites, enhancing Si and Zr diffusivity and leading to dispersed smaller silicides.
